summary: CLI login to internal admin console fails with SSO redirect loop when on corp-proxy
description:
Issue summary:
User cannot authenticate to the internal admin console via the CLI when connected through the corporate HTTP proxy. The CLI starts the browser SSO flow, opens the Okta page, then immediately redirects back to the CLI auth callback and repeats indefinitely (redirect loop).

Impact:
- Multiple platform engineers are unable to access the admin console CLI to manage Dedicated clusters and rollouts.
- Blocker for at least one on-call rotation (cannot respond to a rollout alert).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure system to use the corporate HTTP proxy (proxy.example.redwood.com:8080) via environment variables (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY).
2) Run `redwood-cli login --console` which launches browser-based SSO.
3) Complete Okta authentication in browser.
4) Observe immediate redirect back to CLI auth handler and the flow restarts repeatedly.

Observed logs (CLI verbose):
- Received authorization code, exchanging for token...
- Callback received from https://internal-console.redwood.com/_auth/callback?code=ABC123
- Validating state and session cookie... status=302 Location: /_auth/start?error=redirect_loop
- Initiating new auth flow

Expected behavior:
- After successful Okta auth, CLI receives token and user is logged in.

Notes:
- Web console (browser without proxy) works fine. Problem only reproducible when the machine is configured to use the corporate proxy.
- Several affected users are on macOS and Linux; VPNless machines behind the proxy are impacted.
comments: Maya Patel (Reporter) [2026-03-10]: Hit this during incident drilling. Can reproduce consistently on my dev laptop when HTTP_PROXY is set. Web UI login works if I bypass the proxy. CLI is stuck in loop. Escalating to SRE.
Support Triage (Ruth Alvarez) [2026-03-10]: Marked P1. Assigning to Ethan. Collecting browser and proxy logs. Asking affected users for proxy request traces and Okta transaction IDs.

Ethan Liang (Assignee) [2026-03-11]: Initial hypothesis: proxy is stripping or rewriting the session cookie or Altering redirect headers (X-Forwarded-For/X-Forwarded-Proto). Requested proxy team to capture raw request/response for the auth callback path. Also requested Okta debug logs for the recent auth attempts (transaction IDs provided).

Proxy Team (Jordan Kim) [2026-03-11]: Captured tcpdump and proxy access logs. Found that the corporate proxy inserts a 'Via' header and normalizes Set-Cookie attributes, removing 'SameSite=None; Secure' on the auth cookie when rewriting responses for HTTP->HTTPS redirects. Suspect cookie becomes unusable in the callback, causing server to start a fresh auth flow.

SRE (Leah Morgan) [2026-03-12]: Confirmed server sees callback but missing session cookie. Reproduced by running a local mitm proxy simulating corporate proxy behavior; when SameSite or Secure is stripped, console rejects the session and re-initiates auth. Preparing hotfix to tolerate missing cookie for CLI flow and log detailed diagnostic info.

Maya Patel (Reporter) [2026-03-12]: Workaround (bypassing proxy) allowed me to complete the login and clear the alert. Leaving laptop off the proxy is disruptive but workable for now. Please advise on permanent fix.

Ethan Liang (Assignee) [2026-03-12]: Will deploy configuration change to gateway to preserve Set-Cookie attributes for the auth domain and implement server-side fallback for CLI auth within next 24 hours. Opening follow-up to update runbook.

Proxy Team (Jordan Kim) [2026-03-12]: Gateway change rolled out to preserve cookie attributes for *.redwood.com domain. Observed successful auth flow from test machines. Requesting monitoring for 48 hours.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Reproduced with HTTP_PROXY set. Browser completes Okta login but server treats callback as new session. No obvious errors on Okta side beyond expected success. Okta transaction IDs: okta|txn|20260310|7b9f.

2026-03-11: Proxy captured rewrite behavior. Set-Cookie header values truncated; SameSite and Secure flags removed in responses for HTTP->HTTPS bounce through proxy. Proxy access log sample: GET /_auth/callback?code=... 302 - 11ms via proxy-host-01.

2026-03-11: Server logs show missing session cookie at callback handler: session_id=null. Server responds with 302 to /_auth/start to re-initiate flow. CLI log indicates it receives the 302 and restarts flow repeatedly.

2026-03-11: Hypothesis A: Proxy is modifying cookie headers causing session loss. Hypothesis B: Proxy is changing referrer/host headers causing CSRF token mismatch. Evidence favors A based on header diffs.

2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation test: configured proxy to preserve Set-Cookie for internal-console.redwood.com. Test auth with CLI passed. Need production rollout and server-side hardening to avoid tight dependency on SameSite for CLI flows.
Related artifacts: Slack thread #support-auth-462199, tcpdump saved at s3://redwood-support/diag/INT-462199/tcpdump.pcap, okta debug export at gs://okta-debug/okta-20260310-7b9f.log
resolution:
Workaround: Affected users can bypass corporate HTTP proxy temporarily (unset HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY) or use a machine with direct egress to complete CLI login.

Short-term fix (deployed 2026-03-12): Proxy gateway configuration updated to preserve Set-Cookie attributes (SameSite and Secure) for auth traffic to *.redwood.com. Verified successful CLI SSO flow from 5 test hosts.

Planned follow-ups:
- INT-462200 (follow-up): Add server-side fallback to accept ephemeral token exchange for CLI auth when cookie is missing to avoid redirect loops.
- Update runbook: doc link below.
- Monitor: proxy and auth metrics for 48h, endpoints instrumented to log missing cookie occurrences.

Status: Partial fix deployed and verified; monitoring in progress. Ticket remains open until 48h monitor window completes and follow-up INT-462200 is implemented.
